about.name: Qiyu Li
paragraphs: I build AI-native tools and creative software around thinking, creating, and working with AI — mostly around human–AI interaction, visual systems, and turning messy ideas into things that actually work.
Outside the editor you'll usually find me around photography, films, table tennis, and whatever I'm curious about next.

principles: Human judgment stays in the loop.
Build the tools I wish already existed.

_photobandNote: Photographs must live in assets/photography/. Keep native aspect ratios; the band scales, never crops. Titles and exposure lines are plain ASCII because the embedded bitmap face has a limited subset.

lines: Building tools for thinking, creating, and working with AI.
Turning messy ideas into systems that actually run.
Always building something I wish already existed.

_motionNote: Per-component switches so layout stays the author's decision. Each module has its OWN effect — 01 lights indicator keys, rhythm flickers at its meter ceilings, languages sweeps, the two list panels share a row highlight because they are a matched pair, contributions runs a diagonal wave, work marches a selection marquee. `ambient: false` keeps entrances but stops the never-ending ones; `enabled: false` makes the whole page static. Every animated file also carries a prefers-reduced-motion guard, and no effect may start from opacity 0 — see lib/motion.mjs.
_contactNote: A README cannot run script — GitHub strips it — so copy-to-clipboard on click is not possible on this page. EMAIL uses mailto:, which hands the click to whatever the reader's machine uses for mail without printing the address as text. WECHAT links to a QR stripped of the avatar, display name and city that came with it. WEBSITE stays off until yunmin311.github.io actually serves something; it currently 404s.
fortunes: The tool you keep meaning to build is the one you need most.
A system nobody can explain is a system nobody can fix.
Autocomplete is not agreement.
Ship the ugly version. The pretty one never arrives on its own.
Every abstraction is a promise you will have to keep later.
If it only works when you are watching, it does not work.
Good defaults beat good documentation.
The messy draft already knows what the clean one is trying to say.
A model can hold the context. It cannot hold the responsibility.
Name it badly and you will build it badly.
Delete the feature you keep apologising for.
The best interface is the one you stop noticing.
Constraints are the part of the brief that survives contact with reality.
You cannot automate a decision you have never made by hand.
Any pipeline long enough contains one step nobody understands.
Taste is just the errors you have already made, remembered.
If the demo needs narration, the design is not finished.
Prototypes are arguments. Ship the one that wins.
Most 'AI problems' are unclear-input problems wearing a costume.
Two hours of naming things saves two weeks of explaining them.
_cardOverridesNote: THE WORDS ON A SELECTED WORK CARD, and nothing else. WHICH cards appear, and in what order, is decided by the PINNED REPOSITORIES on the GitHub profile — change them at github.com/yunmin311 -> Customize your pins, and the next rebuild follows. Nothing here can add, remove or reorder a card. HOW THE TWO HALVES SPLIT: `name`, `why` and `tags` are curated here, because a sentence worth reading is written by a person; membership, order, `url` and the fallback text come from GitHub. A pin with NO entry here is not an error and needs no code change — its card is built from the repository's own description, primary language and topics, and the build log names it under 'unedited pins' so the wording can be chosen later. Keeping an entry for a project that is not currently pinned is fine and useful: pin it again and the good copy is waiting. `languages` is three-state and optional: 'count' (the default) contributes to LANGUAGE SIGNAL, 'exclude' is real code but generated or vendored so it would distort the mix, 'n/a' is nothing comparable to count at all. Only `languages` still needs a second list's worth of intent, and it is a per-card opt-out rather than a scope.
_dynamicNote: WHAT IS DYNAMIC HERE, IN ONE PLACE: the set of cards (the pins), their order (the pin order), the url and repo behind each, LANGUAGE SIGNAL's numbers, and LANGUAGE SIGNAL's scope — which is exactly the pinned set. WHAT IS CURATED: every hand-written word, which lives in `cardOverrides` below and changes only when this file is edited.

yunmin311/context-distiller.name: Context Distiller
yunmin311/context-distiller.why: Choosing what an AI gets to see is the step nobody built a tool for. A workspace for picking, grouping and compiling that context into one plain-text message — locally, and never sent anywhere.

yunmin311/governance-framework.name: Governance Framework
yunmin311/governance-framework.why: Run several AI agents and they forget, contradict each other, and disagree about which file is real. Pinning the facts into files fixes what a smarter model cannot.

yunmin311/yunmin-workbench.name: Yunmin Workbench
yunmin311/yunmin-workbench.why: A clean-room desktop workbench for running Claude Code and Codex side by side — rebuilt from a frozen baseline rather than patched forward, because a tool you depend on has to be explainable.

yunmin311/dsh-universal-palette.name: DSH Universal Palette
yunmin311/dsh-universal-palette.why: Three products with three different colour systems, and a designer retyping hex codes between them. One plugin turns whatever you are looking at into the palette you actually use.

yunmin311/window-annotator.name: Window Annotator
yunmin311/window-annotator.why: Drawing on the thing you are looking at should not depend on the app supporting it. Hand-drawn marks pin to any Windows window and follow it as it moves, resizes and scrolls.

yunmin311/zheng-tally-obsidian.name: Zheng Tally for Obsidian
yunmin311/zheng-tally-obsidian.why: Counting things in a note should not mean leaving the note. Tally marks you can strike through inline, with the running total kept where the writing happens.

yunmin311/work-capsule.name: Work Capsule
yunmin311/work-capsule.why: Keeping work in sync across machines should not risk it. One click pulls, optionally commits and pushes every folder you chose — fast-forward only, never rewriting history.

yunmin311/pixel-panels.name: Pixel Panels
yunmin311/pixel-panels.why: The components this page is built from, lifted out and documented. One 2px grid, one embedded bitmap face, and the four rules that keep fourteen separate parts reading as a single instrument.

yunmin311/DenseGPT.name: DenseGPT
yunmin311/DenseGPT.why: A long answer you cannot scan is a long answer nobody reads. One stylesheet tightens the reading layout and the content width; a companion spec asks the model for answers shaped to fit it.

_languageScopeNote: HOW the language chart counts. Its SCOPE is not configured — it is the pinned repositories, derived by lib/projects.mjs, so there is no repository list to keep in sync here or anywhere else. `identities` is matched case-insensitively against each commit's author email AND name; add an entry when a new machine commits under a different address, or those commits disappear from the chart with no error at all — the quietest way this panel can be wrong. `exclude` drops generated and vendored languages from the line count: the chart claims 'lines I wrote', and markup or lockfile churn is not writing. `method` is 'authored-lines' (clone each pinned repo, count my insertions); 'bytes' is an explicit escape hatch that measures something different, so it is never selected automatically.
